description: A Line Graph is an essential part of Data Interpretation that shows changes or trends in data over time. In this, individual data points are connected by straight lines.

sections.title: Basic Concepts
sections.description: Understanding the structure of a line graph and its main components.

key_concepts.explanation: The X-axis usually represents time or an independent variable, while the Y-axis represents value or a dependent variable.
A specific point on the graph that represents the intersection of the X and Y values.
The direction of the line showing whether the value is increasing, decreasing, or constant over a period.

sections.title: Essential Formulas for Calculation
sections.description: Mathematical formulas frequently used to solve line graph questions.

equations: Percentage Increase = [(New Value - Old Value) / Old Value] * 100
Percentage Decrease = [(Old Value - New Value) / Old Value] * 100
Average = Sum of all values / Total number of values

sections.title: Steps to Read the Graph
sections.description: A step-by-step guide to extract data accurately and solve questions.

steps.title: Check Title and Scale
steps.detail: Understand the subject of the graph and carefully read the scale and units given on both axes.

steps.title: Extract Data
steps.detail: Read exact values from the relevant points according to the question. If a point lies between grid lines, make a logical estimate.

steps.title: Calculate
steps.detail: Apply the required mathematical formulas to the extracted data to obtain the final answer.

sections.title: Types of Line Graphs
sections.description: Different types of line graphs and their characteristics.

results: Only one variable is studied over a period of time.
Allows for easy data extraction and clear trend analysis.
Two or more variables are compared simultaneously in a single graph.
Reading the legend carefully is essential to avoid confusion between different lines.

sections.title: Common Mistakes and Tips
sections.description: How to avoid common errors made while solving data interpretation questions.

key_concepts.explanation: Sometimes the Y-axis does not start from zero, which can make small numerical differences appear visually exaggerated on the graph.
Always ensure the unit asked in the question and the unit given in the graph (e.g., thousands, millions) are identical before calculating.

cases.condition: When lines intersect in a multiple line graph
results: At that specific point, the value of both variables is exactly equal.
Identifying these intersections is highly important for answering comparative questions efficiently.
